newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers, bosses, start new round of talks.
newsitem.headline: French truckers, bosses, start new round of talks.

text.p: Striking truck drivers and their bosses began a sixth round of talks on Tuesday as truckers tightened their stranglehold on French highways and fuel supplies for the ninth day to press their demands.

Government mediator Robert Cros convened the talks at 3.30 p.m. (1430 GMT) after reporting "significant progress" in earlier rounds focussing on truckers' demands for a pay rise, shorter working hours and earlier retirement.
Union officials told reporters before the talks resumed that the negotiations had yet to deal with their main demands.
"The question is whether the bosses and the government want to resolve the problem politically," said Michel Caillaud of the national drivers' federation.
Haulage companies' spokesman Jehan de Marne said employers were "ready to make concessions" but the demand for a wage rise was unacceptable.

Drivers were manning 176 roadblocks across the provinces on Tuesday, and unions said the popular protest was growing in strength and piling pressure on the economy. The south and west were most seriously affected.
